## 39. The curator's watch — the governance half of §8's first question, and the queue keys on the act that would falsify a cell

**Ticket [#125](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/125).** §8's open question 1 — *"who
revises the sensitive list, on what trigger, and how often?"* — is the last surviving half of the map's
port-set fog. #21 settled the **evidence**; nobody has settled the **governance**. This section settles
it, and settles with it the **watch-list axis** question that
[ADR-0032](../adr/0032-an-evidence-standard-attaches-to-a-table-not-to-a-rule.md) §8 has carried since
it was written and that §27.14 and §31.12 have twice routed here.

**Nothing in this section is a retrieval.** Every fact it uses is already in this note, in a sibling
note, or in an ADR, and every one is cited to the section that measured it. **No row, class, tier or
coverage figure moves**; §4.6 gains one entry and it is the discharge of §38.14's backlog rather than a
new candidate. The reasoning is [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-a-watch-keys-on-the-act-that-would-falsify-a-cell.md).

### 39.1 The three questions, answered in one line each

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| **Who revises a curated table** | **The release** — an act, not a person. The party is the **project**, never the operator; the instrument is a **gate on the edit**, not a standing duty on somebody |
| **On what watch** | **Two instruments**: a **gate** over what is *closed* — eleven checks, run to completion over the table as edited — and a **queue** over what is *open*, which cannot terminate and is therefore sampled |
| **What the watch list keys on** | **The revision act** — the smallest act by the owner that would falsify the cell, and whether that act publishes a notice we read. Five rungs, read off the artefact. **Not the footing tier**, which grades something else |

### 39.2 Why the count has been useless five times, and it is not a reader problem

The sequence is **3 → 2 → 3 → 2 → 3** — `5432`/`5984`/`9042`, then `5432`/`5984`, then `+10255`, then
`−10255`, then `+10248` — with the membership changing at every step. §8 has now carried the rider
*compare members, not counts* on three separate amendments, which is a strong signal that the **unit**
is wrong rather than that three readers were careless.

**It is the unit.** The list enumerates **rows**, and what changes is a **cell's supporting artefact**.
When `10255` left and `10248` joined, two supports moved and the count did not. A row list cannot show
that; nor can it show that **four pairs sit on one sentence** — §16.7 records that `139/tcp`, `137/udp`
and `138/udp` are *"carried by the same Microsoft sentence as `445` and sit inside that row's cell"*,
and §13.1 measures that **none of the four has a configuration artefact to fall back on**. That is the
largest single concentration of exposure in the table and it is invisible on a list of rows.

> **The unit is a `(cell, artefact, revision act)` triple.** A row may be an item twice on two cells;
> four pairs may be one item on one sentence. **The queue's length is barred from being quoted as an
> indicator**, and the queue is published as members with their acts.

### 39.3 The axis — five candidates, one key, and the other four have jobs

The five candidates are **tier · evidence age · support count · artefact class · contradiction by the
owner's own product documentation**. Nobody could propose a measurement for any of them, and the reason
is that nobody had said what the list is **for**.

**It is the order in which a finite reading budget is spent.** The gate exhausts everything that
terminates; what is left is reading somebody else's corpus, which never terminates. So the list must
key on *the probability that a ground has moved with nothing saying so, per unit of reading* — which is
**volatility**, and volatility is a property of the **artefact**.

| Axis | Job |
| --- | --- |
| **Artefact class** | **The key** — read as the **revision act**, never as a prestige ranking |
| Footing tier | **The disclosure.** It grades **evidential distance** (ADR-0059) — the premises the reader supplies. Nothing in that quantity is about how easily the sentence can be edited |
| Evidence age | **The gate's bound and the queue's tie-break**, measured in the **owner's release line** — never first-seen date and never our edit cadence |
| Support count | **The filter.** It decides *whether* a cell is exposed, not where it sits |
| Contradiction by the owner's own product documentation | **Not on the queue at all.** It fires on a row that is **already wrong**, so it is a gate check (G6) |

**The measurement that decides it, from cells already in this note.** Tier and rung disagree, and they
disagree in the direction that matters:

| Pair | Footing tier | Rung | The artefact, and the act that would falsify the cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `10248/tcp` kubelet healthz | **weak** | **1** | `healthzBindAddress: "127.0.0.1"` in a published config-API doc comment — *"a Go source file's comment, which one contributor can change in one commit without any release note"* (§27.5, §27.12) |
| `445/tcp` + `139/tcp` + `137/udp` + `138/udp` | **prohibition** | **2** | One Microsoft page, continuously published with no version pin (`ms.date` 2024-10-25). **[measured] §13.1: there is no configuration artefact behind any of the four** |
| `623/udp` IPMI | **prohibition** | **2** | Dell's and HPE's own default-value documentation; a BMC's configuration is firmware, so §13.1 records nothing to open. **[measured] §36.7: this row has already been de-attested once** — §28.9's direction disposal had to be *"re-founded on a current artefact, HPE having retired *Insight Online direct connect*"* |
| `2379`, `2380/tcp` etcd | **prohibition** | **2** | `THREAT_MODEL.md` at `etcd-io/etcd` `v3.7.1` — three months old and absent from the `3.5` and `3.6` lines (§15.9) |
| `5432/tcp` PostgreSQL | **weak** | **3** | `listen_addresses` in `postgresql.conf.sample`, moving only in a release with a version and a changelog |

> **The top tier holds the more volatile artefacts here and the weak tier holds the more stable one.**
> A list keyed on tier spends the reading budget close to backwards. That is why its count has meant
> nothing five times running — it was measuring the wrong quantity, so its movement carried no
> information about the right one.

**The rungs**, read off the artefact and never off what the sentence says:

| Rung | The act | Announced? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | A source comment, an unversioned page, or a dataset with no successor — one contributor, one commit, **nothing rendered changes** | No, and invisible even to a reader of the owner's rendered documentation |
| **2** | A continuously-published page with no version pin, or a documentation branch tracking a release line — one contributor, one commit | No release note; the page simply reads differently tomorrow |
| **3** | A **shipped configuration default** — changes only in a software release | Announced by a version we can pin and diff |
| **4** | **Issued prose in a versioned documentation set** | Announced, and the prior version stays retrievable |
| **5** | A **specification** — a new document with a new number | Announced, and never silently |

**The filter is support count, and it explains a correction this note made for the wrong stated
reason.** §17.6 already joins the halves — *"Every row in it rests on a negative … so every one is
**sole-ground** and every one is **exposed**"* — and
[ADR-0046](../adr/0046-a-negatives-corpus-is-its-owners-class-list-and-only-a-sole-ground-negative-is-exposed.md)
limb 1 says only a sole-ground negative is exposed. Read on the positive side: a cell carried by two
**independent** artefacts needs **two** acts to fall, so it is not exposed.

> **`10255/tcp` came off the watch list at §18.6 because it joined the prohibition tier. The reason it
> actually stopped being exposed is that it acquired a *second ground*** — if `security-checklist.md`'s
> line goes, the row falls back to `readOnlyPort: 0` and **demotes a tier rather than losing a cell**.
> #88's rider *"both kubelet cells are now exposed to its mirror"* is **answered and refused**:
> exposure to a demotion is not exposure to de-attestation. Tier was taking credit for work support
> count was doing, which is the same confusion in the disarming direction.
>
> > **Confirmed and re-sited at the cell by §41** ([#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135),
> > [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-a-second-ground-counts-only-where-it-would-have-carried-the-cells-proposition-alone.md)).
> > **The reasoning above is right, and it is about `10255`'s FOOTING cell rather than about the row.**
> > A footing tier grades **evidential distance** and is authored by us, so an owner's act cannot falsify
> > it; the fallback yields the same **proposition** at a lower tier and the act demotes. What the
> > paragraph does not license is disposing of a **row**: `10250`'s footing cell is disposed of the same
> > way and its **claim** cell is not, being sole-ground on the `Used By` cell (§19.12). #88's rider is
> > therefore still refused **for the two footing cells** and is **live for `10255`'s claim cell**, which
> > no section has tested — §41.7 flags it for [#134](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/134).

**A corroborator is never a ground**, so it can never remove an item — §2.3, applied at §39.5 to
`2375/tcp`.

> **The bar a ground must clear is fixed by §41** ([#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135)).
> *Carries the same cell* means **would have yielded the cell's proposition standing alone**, tested per
> **cell** and never per row: *exists* is not enough, and *at the same tier* is too much. §41.2 states
> the four-step test.

### 39.4 The queue as of evidence already held — ~~eight items~~ **nine since §41**, and ~~two~~ **three** of the pairs it adds are top-tier

**Provisional, and marked as such.** The per-cell independence test has been run only over the cells
this note has already measured; the full pass over all 38 pairs plus the frequency half is a ticket
(§39.9). Every ground below is cited to the section that measured it, and **nothing here is retrieved**.

| # | Rung | Item — `(cell, artefact, revision act)` | Pairs | Ground |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **1** | `10248`'s footing @ the config-API doc comment — one contributor, one commit, no release note | `10248/tcp` | §27.5, §27.12: a restricting `healthzBindAddress` *"and nothing else"*; `security-checklist.md` does not name the port |
| 2 | **1** | `verge-core`'s frequency half @ `nmap-services` — a **cure-availability** item: a third party publishing replacement frequency data, never announced to us | — | ADR-0038: a product failing the reach test, *"stays, watched"*; the replacement hunt is closed **on capability** |
| 3 | **2** | The SMB cell @ one Microsoft page — one commit, no version pin | `445/tcp`, `139/tcp`, `137/udp`, `138/udp` | §16.7 (one sentence, four pairs), §13.1 (**no configuration artefact**) |
| 4 | **2** | `623`'s footing @ Dell's and HPE's default-value documentation | `623/udp` | §13.1 as qualified by §28; **§36.7 — already de-attested once** |
| 5 | **2** | etcd's prohibition cell @ `THREAT_MODEL.md` | `2379/tcp`, `2380/tcp` | §16.3, §15.9 — three months old, absent from two live release lines |
| 6 | **3** | `5432`'s footing @ `postgresql.conf.sample` | `5432/tcp` | §4.5 — *"the one service surveyed whose upstream documentation states no position at all"* |
| 7 | **3** | `5984`'s footing @ CouchDB's `default.ini` | `5984/tcp` | §13.2; a restricting shipped default and no owner prose |
| 8 | **5** | `certificate-expiring`'s fraction @ RFC 9773 §1 on form and the issuer's published lifetime schedule on value | — | ADR-0038 scopes ADR-0034's *"nothing to watch"*: the fraction removes the **quantity**, never the **attestation** |

~~**Eight items over ten `(port, transport)` pairs and two non-port cells**~~ **— NINE items over ELEVEN
pairs and two non-port cells since §41** ([#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135)),
against a three-row list — and ~~two~~ **three** of the pairs it adds sit in the *top* footing tier. The
eight items above stand unchanged with their grounds and their rungs; **item 9 is `10250`'s claim cell**
and is stated at §41.4.

**Not on the queue, each with its reason:**

| Not an item | Why |
| --- | --- |
| ~~`10250/tcp`, `10255/tcp`~~ | ~~A second independent ground exists, so the act **demotes** rather than de-attests (§39.3)~~ — **SUPERSEDED at this clause by §41** ([#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135), [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-a-second-ground-counts-only-where-it-would-have-carried-the-cells-proposition-alone.md)). **The disposal was made at the ROW; the unit is the CELL.** It is right for both **footing** cells — §18.7 measures `10250` falling back to the scoping tier and `10255` to the weak tier, so the proposition survives and the act demotes. It is **wrong for `10250`'s claim cell**: **[measured]** §19.12 records *"Claim 3 has **no second support** on this row"*, so that cell is sole-ground and is **queue item 9** — §41.3 |
| `certificate-weak-key-or-signature`'s whole table | **[measured]** [`weak-key-and-signature.md`](./weak-key-and-signature.md) §9.3 — the residue is a **scope** weakness and *"no shipped default is involved, so **silent de-attestation cannot reach them**"*. Its cure-availability item, SP 800-131A Rev. 3 going final, sits at rung 5 and is announced |
| Every graded row with an owner sentence **and** a configuration artefact | Two independent acts are needed. This is most of the list, which is why the queue is short |
| The count of anything | Barred as an indicator — §39.2 |

**The queue is a superset of the weak tier.** All three weak-tier rows stay on it, so this ruling takes
nothing off anybody's attention; it only adds. That is what makes it cheap in the one direction that
could cost something.

### 39.5 §38.14's backlog, discharged — and §4.6 gains one entry

**1. `9443/tcp` enters §4.6, and the table is 24 entries.** §38.14 item 1 refused it *"on §37.11's
disposal for a port no section proposed"* — but §37.11's disposal of `9443` was *"**Not a subject.** No
owner takes a placement position"*, and **§38.14 itself measured that Elastic does take one**, in the
affirming direction: *"Outbound from Elastic over the public internet to your cluster's endpoint"*
(`remote-clusters.md`, `applies_to: ece/eck/ess/self: ga`), with the same page numbering `9443` for
API-key remote clusters. **A citation to a disposal the citing section has just refuted does not carry
it.** `9443` was examined and definitively refused on the **claim gate**, which is precisely what §4.6
holds since §24 — `10256`, `10258`, `1433`, `9200`, `9300` are all there on the same gate.

> | Excluded | The ground |
> |---|---|
> | **`9443/tcp` Elasticsearch remote cluster server** | **Claim 3 fails on §10.3's own failure condition, met on arrival, and no other claim in the closed set fits.** The pair is Claim 3-shaped on its face — *"a dedicated server port … for communication between clusters"* (`remote-clusters.md`, `v9.5.1`, where `remote_cluster.port` *"Defaults to `9443`"*) — and Elastic names the public internet as the **supported** connection path for exactly that traffic in the same corpus: *"\| {{ech}} deployment \| Self-managed cluster in your network \| **Outbound from Elastic over the public internet to your cluster's endpoint.** Allow the connection with IP-based rules on your side. \|"*. **Claim 1** and **Claim 2** are unavailable on `9200`'s measurements at `v9.5.1` (§38.6), the security and TLS settings being cluster-wide rather than per-interface. §38.14 item 1, §39.5 |

**The refusal is bounded on arrival** and adds nothing to §17.1's exposed population: the owner points
**the other way** rather than being silent, so it is not a negative at all — `10258`'s shape (§27.7).
**No `(port, transport)` pair moves and the list stays at 38.** Its determinacy verdict is unread and
unreached, exactly as for `9200` and `9300`.

**2. `2375/tcp`'s third-party corroborator changes nothing, and the new instrument says why.** §38.14
item 4 recorded Elastic placing `2375` on-host for internal Docker communication and did not act.
Correct, and now for a stated reason rather than a policy: **§2.3 bars a corroborator from being a
ground, and the queue's filter counts grounds** — so a corroborator can neither carry a cell nor
**remove it from the queue**. `2375/tcp` is unaffected in both directions. Recorded because the
symmetry is not obvious: it is tempting to read a second party's agreement as a second support, and it
is not one.

**3. The docs-source comment is a new hazard shape, and it earns a standing rule and a gate check.**
§38.14 item 6 and §38.16 record a `%` source comment in `elastic/docs-content` saying the opposite of
§38.5's finding, invisible in the rendered page, refused under
[ADR-0045](../adr/0045-an-owners-documentation-is-what-it-has-issued.md) because a comment in a docs
source is not **issued**. The refusal is right and the shape is general:

> **An owner's *unrendered* bytes are not issued.** A retrieval that reads raw source must state
> whether the string it quotes is **present in the owner's rendered artefact**. A session reading
> rendered HTML never meets an unrendered string; a session reading raw bytes meets it and, without
> the marker, quotes it. This is a **rider on ADR-0045**, not a new gate — issuance was already the
> test, and what is new is that the raw-bytes route makes the test **skippable by accident**.

It becomes gate check **G7** (§39.6). It is also the reason §38.16's corpus-grep method — *"read the
corpus, not the page list"*, which is what found the sentence that decided `9200` — needs a rider
rather than a warning: the method is right and it enlarges the set of strings a session can quote that
the owner has not published.

### 39.6 The gate — eleven checks, all closed, run over the table as edited

**A check is *closed* where its population is enumerable and its evidence is bytes the project already
holds, plus a finite named set of targeted re-fetches.** It terminates, so it runs to completion. **An
edit to a curated table is complete only when the gate is green over the post-edit state** — the gate
blocks the *edit*, never the release.

| # | Check | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **G1** | A row's footing tier agrees with its class where the two are coupled | defect — [#83](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/83) |
| **G2** | Every graded footing cell has been walked against the tier criterion **as it currently stands**, and the walk's date is at or after the criterion's last amendment. **Its population is the criterion's DOMAIN — the two graded tiers, 24 cells, and NOT all 27 footing cells: the weak tier is outside the domain, the criterion reading an owner statement and a weak cell having none ([#154](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/154), §46)** | defect — [#93](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/93), [#98](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/98), [#101](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/101), [#107](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/107); **and triggers 3 and 6, which are this check read at two moments** |
| **G3** | No row rests on an owner's documented hard failure its shipped bytes do not enforce | defect — [#92](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/92) |
| **G4** | No sentence the edit supersedes stands unmarked anywhere the edit's terms occur, **the edited file included** | defect — [ADR-0058](../adr/0058-a-superseded-mechanism-is-withdrawn-at-the-site-that-specifies-it.md), [#102](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/102), [#106](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/106) |
| **G5** | No exclusion's stated ground has been withdrawn | defect — [#104](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/104) |
| **G6** | No artefact **already held** carries an owner affirmation defeating a held row | defect — [#109](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/109), [#112](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/112), [#114](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/114). Grepping a corpus we already downloaded is closed; **finding a new one is a queue item** |
| **G7** | Every quotation retrieved from **raw source bytes** is present in the owner's **rendered** artefact | trigger — **new**, §39.5 item 3 |
| **G8** | Every citation resolves, and its quoted string is still a **token** of the artefact at the tag named. ~~*(population unnamed)*~~ **Its population is named at §44** ([#150](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/150), [ADR-0088](../adr/0088-a-re-resolution-check-recurs-only-where-its-target-can-move.md)): **internal** — every relative link, `ADR-00NN`, `§N` and `#N`, no fetch; **G8-entry** — a citation to a **content-addressed** target, checked once by the edit that pins it and never re-fetched; **G8-recurring** — a citation to a **moving** target carrying a **live** cell, **36 members over 30 owners**, listed at §44.4. **A run may not choose a subset**, which is what §40.9 recorded as this row's defect | trigger 5's closed half — §37.14, §38.16; population §44 |
| **G9** | No shipped constant is the product of a fraction and a moving world quantity the subject carries | trigger 4 — [ADR-0034](../adr/0034-derive-the-claim-before-looking-for-the-owner.md), ADR-0038 limb 3 |
| **G10** | Every document refused as **unissued** is re-tested for issuance | trigger 7 — ADR-0045, [#86](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/86). A targeted re-fetch over a named list, currently of one |
| **G11** | For every footing cell, the owner's **current release tag** against the tag the cell was read at; a difference marks the cell **stale-against-tag** | trigger 2's closed half, and the queue's tie-break |

**The six detectable defects and five of the eight triggers are one instrument**, and the reason the
two lists looked like different kinds of thing is that nobody had asked which of them **terminates**.
The defect list is six and not five — §38 added the sixth — and *five* was itself a superseded figure
standing in the present tense, which is G4's own shape found on the sentence that enumerates G4.

**Which of the eight triggers a release can actually check:**

| Trigger | Release? |
| --- | --- |
| A footing never checked against the standard it is now held to | **Completely** — G2 |
| A footing move re-arming the class sweep | **Completely** — G2, the same check at a later moment |
| Silent staleness | **Completely** — G9 |
| A drafted document becoming issued | **Completely** — G10, and it is the cheapest because the owner announces it |
| A protocol changing shipped defaults | **Half** — G11 sees the **tag** move; whether the default moved needs reading |
| Citation staleness on a different cadence from content | **Half** — G8 sees *resolves* and *still occurs*; #110's instance, a citation firing on a **feature name**, needs reading |
| A primary source changing its position | **Not at all** — queue |
| A competing owner starting or stopping documenting its service | **Not at all** — queue, and it is narrow: only rows resting on convention (ADR-0042) |

> **A release can check what terminates and can check nothing else. What it cannot do is notice that an
> owner changed its mind — that needs reading, and reading is what the queue rations.**

**G11 is where *evidence age* lands.** *This footing was read at `v1.34.1` and the owner is at
`v1.37.0`* is a fact about the subject in the subject's own units and is mechanically checkable.
*This footing is fourteen months old* is a fact about **us**:
[ADR-0043](../adr/0043-a-clock-reading-rule-bounds-its-evidence-in-the-subjects-own-units.md)'s
refusal exactly. **[measured]** §37.11 item 5 already ran G11 by hand and recorded the result without
naming it — `security-checklist.md` unmodified since **2025-02-28** against releases through
**v1.37.0-rc.0** — and correctly declined to treat it as staleness, because a document that has not
changed is not thereby stale. G11 marks the cell; it does not condemn it.

**A machine may raise; only a release may rule.** Every check above is mechanical enough to automate
and none of them may **act**: moving a row authors a claim, and §2.2's first sentence bars us from
asserting one; ADR-0037 limb 2 adds that a row moves only on a retrieval scoped to the row. The
watch's output is a **question** — *this cell's artefact has moved past the tag it was read at; is the
cell still true?* — and the answer is a retrieval, which is a ticket.

**What a release owes the queue is a disclosure, never a quantum.** No number of items per release is
set: a quantum manufactures a figure nobody can attest (ADR-0034), and it would restore meaning to the
queue's **length**, which is the failure being repaired. What is owed is
[ADR-0040](../adr/0040-a-specifications-silence-is-not-the-owners-silence.md)'s **bounded residue** —
the queue's head, how far down it read, and what it did not read, falsifiable by naming one item.

### 39.7 A withdrawal that supplies no replacement does not hold — the nineteen sites, marked

**[measured]** ADR-0038 withdrew *watch list = weak tier* — *"§8's watch list is redefined by shape,
not by cause"* — and [#102](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/102) wrote that withdrawal
into ADR-0032 §8 itself. **The identity nonetheless stands as a reason or a rule at nineteen sites** —
fifteen in this note and four in ADRs, one of them in ADR-0032 §8's own body:

| Where | The clause |
| --- | --- |
| §1's merge-reconciliation table | *"the weak tier is the watch list"* |
| §2.2's `#95` amendment | *"…and §8's watch list **grows with it**"* |
| §13.4 | *"…what §4.5 and the map's curation patch both lean on when they **call the weak tier a watch list**"* |
| §13.7 | *"the map's curation patch **reads the weak tier as the curator's watch list**"* |
| §16's ruling box | *"…so the watch list **gains a member**"* |
| §16.8 | *"…names the weak tier as the curator's watch list and **must record three rows** rather than two"* |
| §17.6 | *"the map's curation patch **names the tier as the watch list**"* |
| §17.6's disarming box | *"The weak tier, **and therefore the curator's watch list**, is…"* |
| §18.6 | *"…and §8's watch list **grows with it**"* |
| §18.8 | *"…must record the watch list as **two rows** again"* |
| §27.6 | *"ADR-0032 §8's watch list **moves with it**"* |
| §27.12 | *"The weak tier grew, **so the watch list grew with it**"* |
| §30.2 | *"…and §8's watch list is unchanged **with them**"* |
| §30.8 | *"§27 grew the weak tier, **and the watch list grows with it**"* |
| §31.10 | *"The weak tier does not move, **so the watch list does not**"* |
| **ADR-0032 §8's `#95` box** | *"**The weak tier is the watch list**, so the watch list grows with it"* |
| **ADR-0050**'s Consequences | *"**The curator's watch list returns to** `5432/tcp` and `5984/tcp`"* |
| **ADR-0059**'s Consequences | *"The weak tier, **and therefore** ADR-0032 §8's watch list, is unchanged…"* |
| **ADR-0061**'s Consequences | *"ADR-0032 §8's watch list **stays at** `5432/tcp`, `5984/tcp` and `10248/tcp`"* |

**Five further sites *pose* the question rather than asserting the identity, and they are CLOSED
rather than marked** — §27.13 (*"whether the watch list should key on tier or on volatility"*), §31.7
(*"a third candidate axis beside tier and evidence age — artefact class"*), §31.12 (*"trivially
measurable and not obviously the right axis"*), **ADR-0045**'s Consequences (*"whether the watch list
should key on tier or on evidence age is the map's patch"*) and **ADR-0059**'s Rationale (*"a third
candidate axis … reported rather than acted on"*). **§31.7 and ADR-0061 limb 3 named the winner without
knowing it**, and ADR-0061's clause — *"artefact class bears instead on **volatility** … and that is a
different column from the tier"* — is **confirmed rather than marked**: it is this section's ruling
written a ticket early. One further site is superseded **in part**: **ADR-0034**'s *"the port-curation
patch's third input … **does not join the watch list**"*, which is true of the **quantity** and false of
the **attestation** (§39.4 item 8).

**The ADR-0032 site is the sharp one.** It sits **below** #102's withdrawal box in the same section
and carries `#109` and `#114` strike-throughs, which proves it was edited **after** the withdrawal was
written. That is [#106](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/106)'s intra-document shape at
the one sentence the shape was named to protect.

**All nineteen are marked at their clauses.** Bare **enumerations** of the weak tier inside per-pass
figure tables are **not** marked: they are dated records of a *footing tier*, which is a real and
unchanged object, and §16.8's merge convention already reads them as deltas rather than totals. What is
marked is every place the identity appears as a **reason** or a **rule** — ADR-0058's test being
whether the sentence, read alone and in the present tense, would cause a competent session to build the
thing.

> **The diagnosis is not carelessness, and it generalises.** ADR-0038 withdrew the identity and named
> **no successor**. Every subsequent pass had a watch to update and exactly one enumeration to update it
> with, so each reached for the weak tier again and wrote the identity back. **A sentence that names no
> successor is re-derived by the next session that needs one** — so **the repair for a regenerating
> clause is a replacement, not a stronger strike-through**, and a sweep of nineteen sites is worth
> nothing without one. That is why #125 does both in one pass, and it is the half of the diagnosis
> ADR-0058 and #106 do not carry.

### 39.9 Thin ground, flagged per the standing rule

**The queue at §39.4 is provisional and its provisionality is the largest weakness here.** The
independence test — *does a second artefact carry this same cell* — has been run only over the cells
this note has already measured. Two cases are genuinely undetermined and are named rather than assumed:

- **`2379`/`2380`.** §13.6 records `etcd.conf.yml.sample` as *"neither"* operative nor example — *"the
  first that does not declare itself"* — so whether a restricting default is available as a fallback
  ground is exactly what §13.6 left open. If it is, the pair leaves the queue on the same reasoning
  that removed `10255`. **The criterion that would change the verdict** is §12.2's self-declaration
  test run on that file, which is a retrieval this section may not perform.
- **`10250/tcp`.** It is off the queue on the ground that `ports-and-protocols.md`'s `Used By: Self,
  Control plane` cell is a second, independent artefact. §16.9 calls that cell *"the thinnest placement
  in the table"*. A reader who holds that a cell too thin to carry a tier is also too thin to count as a
  **ground** puts `10250` back on the queue at rung 2. That reader is not obviously wrong, and the
  question is a real one: **the filter counts grounds, and nothing yet says a ground must be strong
  enough to have carried the cell alone.**

  > **DISCHARGED by §41** ([#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135),
  > [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-a-second-ground-counts-only-where-it-would-have-carried-the-cells-proposition-alone.md)).
  > **A ground must be strong enough to have carried the cell's *proposition* alone, and the test is run
  > per cell rather than per row** — but *at the same tier* is refused, a tier being our disclosure of
  > evidential distance rather than the owner's assertion. **`10250` goes back on the queue and not on the
  > cell this bullet expected**: its **footing** cell falls back to the scoping tier on the `Used By` cell
  > (§18.7) and stays off; its **claim** cell is sole-ground on that same `Used By` cell — **[measured]**
  > §19.12, *"Claim 3 has no second support on this row"* — and is **queue item 9** at rung 2. The reader
  > above was right about the row and wrong about the cell, and the disposal this bullet doubted had
  > tested a row where the unit is a cell. §41.3.

**The rung ladder is a judgement about artefacts wearing the clothes of a measurement, and the boundary
between rungs 2 and 4 is where it will first fail.** *Continuously published with no version pin* and
*issued in a versioned documentation set* are distinguishable on today's five instances and will not
stay so: a vendor that versions its documentation site and then edits a prior version in place sits in
neither. The ladder survives that by being read off the artefact — *is there a retrievable prior
version?* — which is a question with a byte answer. It is flagged because the first ambiguous case
should be **ticketed rather than decided by whoever meets it**, which is ADR-0061's own precedent.

**Two counts here are of this note's own text rather than of the world**, and they are as good as the
search terms: the **nineteen** identity sites at §39.7 were found by searching for the identity's
connective phrasings (*grows with it*, *moves with it*, *names the tier as*, *reads the weak tier as*,
*therefore the curator's*, *must record the watch list*) plus the literal string, over this note and
ADR-0032. A site phrasing it some other way would not have matched. The **six** defect checks are
counted from [#125](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/125)'s own enumeration, which says
*five* — the discrepancy is the point and is recorded at §39.6, not smoothed.

**The instrument is unmeasured in the direction that matters most.** Nobody has yet run G1–G11 to
completion over the composed table; §39.8 records the two hits G4 produced on the way past. A gate
whose first full run has not happened is a design, and the honest statement is that it is priced at
one pass and has not been paid.

### 39.10 Retrieval method and hazards, recorded per §9.5, §11.9, §12.9, §13.10, §14.6, §16.10, §17.10, §22.10, §30.10, §32.13, §33.11, §36.14, §37.14 and §38.16

- **This section performed no retrieval, and that is a method rather than an omission.** #125 is a
  governance question; every fact it needs was measured by a prior pass and is cited to it. A section
  that re-retrieved would be re-deciding the evidence half, which #21 closed and this ticket is
  explicitly scoped out of.
- **Every quoted string in this section is quoted from this repository**, not from an owner's corpus, so
  G7 is vacuous here and G8 reduces to an internal cross-reference check. Both were run by hand over
  the section's own citations.
- **The one measured claim about the world is second-hand and says so.** *`623/udp` has already been
  de-attested once* is §36.7's measurement, not this section's; what is new is the reading of it as an
  instance of §8's hazard on a top-tier row, which no prior section drew.
- **A sibling pass may be editing this repository concurrently.** This section's delta is not empty —
  §4.6 moves 23 → 24 — so it is stated as a delta and its basis is `main` at `4c7fb50`. **Where §39 and
  §1 disagree, §1 governs.**

## 40. The gate run — G1 through G11 over the composed table, and the baseline every later edit is measured against

**Ticket [#133](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/133).** §39.6 specified an eleven-check
gate and §39.9 recorded, as the instrument's largest weakness, that *"nobody has yet run G1–G11 to
completion over the composed table … a gate whose first full run has not happened is a design, and the
honest statement is that it is priced at one pass and has not been paid."* **This section pays it.**

**What this section is.** A run, not a rule. It mints no ADR, moves no row, no class, no tier and no
coverage figure, and it reopens nothing §39 or §41 settled. What it produces is a **verdict per check**,
an **enumerated defect list**, and — because an edit is complete only when the gate is green over the
post-edit state — **the baseline state against which every later edit's gate run is compared**.

**Four targeted re-fetches were performed**, all inside §39.6's *finite named set*: G10's list of one
(Apache Kafka's `docs/security/security-model.md`), G11's owner release tags, G7's two
rendered-artefact tests, and one G8 string check. Every other check ran over bytes already held.
Where a check could not be completed, it is recorded as **incomplete** with the reason, never as passed.

### 40.1 The result, per check

| # | Check | Verdict | Defects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G1** | Footing tier agrees with class where the two are coupled | **GREEN** | 0 |
| **G2** | Every graded footing cell walked against the tier criterion as it currently stands | **GREEN**, one disclosure | 0 |
| **G3** | No row rests on a documented hard failure the shipped bytes do not enforce | **GREEN** | 0 |
| **G4** | No superseded sentence stands unmarked where the edit's terms occur | **RED** | **11 sites, 3 shapes** |
| **G5** | No exclusion's stated ground has been withdrawn | **RED** | **2 sites, +1 recorded** |
| **G6** | No artefact already held carries an owner affirmation defeating a held row | **GREEN** | 0 |
| **G7** | Every raw-source quotation is present in the owner's rendered artefact | **GREEN**, two precision riders | 0 |
| **G8** | Every citation resolves and its quoted string is still a token at the tag named | **PARTIAL** — internal half complete and green; external half not completable | 0 found |
| **G9** | No shipped constant is the product of a fraction and a moving world quantity | **GREEN**, one disclosure | 0 |
| **G10** | Every document refused as unissued is re-tested for issuance | **GREEN**, re-fetched today | 0 |
| **G11** | Owner's current release tag against the tag the cell was read at | **RED**, and **run to completion over all 27 cells** | **5** — 9 cells stale-against-tag in 4 groups, 1 stale-against-horizon |

> **Eight green, two red, one partial — and the two reds are both `G4`-shaped, one of them literally.**
> **[measured] 18 defects across 11 checks on the first full run**, none of which moves a row and every
> one of which would have gone on regenerating. §39.9's price was one pass; the pass has been paid and
> the instrument earned it.
>
> **Ten of the eleven checks ran to completion; G8 alone did not, and its incompletion is a defect of
> the gate's specification rather than of this run** — §40.9.

### 40.2 G4 — eleven sites in three shapes, every one struck at its clause

[ADR-0058](../adr/0058-a-superseded-mechanism-is-withdrawn-at-the-site-that-specifies-it.md)'s test
throughout: *would this sentence, read alone and in the present tense, cause a competent session to
build the thing?* Bare per-pass figure tables are **not** marked — §39.7's convention, unchanged.

**Shape A — the v1 rule-set denominator, `sixteen` → `seventeen`.** [#128](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/128)
admitted a seventeenth rule and [ADR-0071](../adr/0071-a-vantage-scoped-claim-is-read-only-at-the-vantage-that-scopes-it.md)
wrote *"ADR-0024's sixteen rules becomes seventeen"* — **naming the successor**, which is what §39.7
says a withdrawal needs. It was then written at some sites and not others.

| Site | The clause | Struck |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ADR-0044**, *"No rule loses anything"* | *"one of the **sixteen** rules names a port … the remaining **eleven** read a facet"* | **Yes** — `1 / 4 / 12` of **seventeen** |
| **ADR-0044**, same section | *"not as one of the **sixteen**"* | **Yes** |
| **ADR-0004** §*"Two questions, two documents"* | *"thirteen of the **sixteen** rules have nothing for it to govern"* | **Yes** — the **thirteen** is unchanged; #128's rule carries a curated table |
| **`sensitive-ports.md` §8** question 6's closure | *"thirteen of the **sixteen** v1 rules carry no table at all"* | **Yes** |

> **ADR-0044 is the sharpest site in the whole run, and the reason is in the git history.**
> [`safe-active-probing.md`](./safe-active-probing.md) carries the **same** `1 / 4 / 11` split, copied
> from ADR-0044 — and the 2026-08-15 reconciliation commit *"the aperture statement's rule denominator
> moved to seventeen"* **corrected the copy and did not reach the original**. That is ADR-0058's
> proposition in its purest available form: *a superseded mechanism is withdrawn at the site that
> **specifies** it, not only at the site that **restates** it* — and the correcting session, working the
> restating site, could not see the specifying one. **A reconciliation pass is not a G4 run**, and this
> is the measurement that says so.
>
> **ADR-0004's site is [#106](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/106)'s intra-document
> shape**: the file's own #128 amendment, ninety lines below, reads *"The v1 set is **seventeen**
> rules"*. A document supersedes itself, and this one did not.

**Shape B — a removed row named in the present tense as a list member.**

| Site | The clause | Struck |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`sensitive-ports.md` §8** question **5**, which is **open** | *"When the signal fires on **9200** it is asserting Elasticsearch on a port registered to `wap-wsp`"* | **Yes** — `9200/tcp` was removed by §38 ([#114](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/114)); the question survives on `623/udp` |
| **ADR-0042** Context | *"**`9200/tcp` is on the list.**"* | **Yes** |
| **ADR-0042** Context, next paragraph | *"Read as a squat is fatal, **`9200`, `9300`**, `2181`, `9042`, `10250`, `10255` and `623/udp` all leave the list"* | **Yes** — the puzzle is unaffected and the ADR's answer untouched |

> **ADR-0042 is the same defect as ADR-0044's, one document over.** #114 wrote its amendment into

### 40.6 The baseline, stated explicitly because that is half this section's job

**An edit to a curated table is complete only when the gate is green over the post-edit state** (§39.6).
That sentence has had no referent, because no state had ever been gated. **It has one now.**

> **THE GATE BASELINE, as of [#133](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/133), 2026-08-15.**
> The composed table stands at **38 pairs · classes `12 / 7 / 19` · tiers `13 / 11 / 3` · coverage 27 of
> 38 · §4.6 24 entries · `verge-core` 136 (131 TCP, 5 UDP)**, against a v1 rule set of **17** and **4**
> curated tables. Over that state: **G1, G2, G3, G6, G7, G9, G10 are GREEN. G5 and G11 are RED with
> their defects enumerated at §40.3 and §40.4. G4 is GREEN as of this section's own edits and was RED on
> arrival at eleven sites. G8's internal half is GREEN and its external half is UNRUN.**
>
> **A later edit's gate run is compared to this.** A check that was green here and is red there was
> broken by that edit. A check that was red here and is red there is **inherited**, not caused —
> and the two must not be confused, which is the only reason a baseline is worth writing down.

**What a green gate does not mean.** Seven greens over this table are seven statements about **bytes
this project holds**, not about the world. G6 grepped a corpus; it did not go looking. G8's external
half is exactly the reading the queue rations. **The gate's completeness is a completeness of
population, never of enquiry** — which is §39.6's own partition, now measured from the inside.

### 40.7 One incidental hit, outside the eleven, and it belongs to #135's ruling rather than to a check

**`5432/tcp` may not be a queue item, and [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-a-second-ground-counts-only-where-it-would-have-carried-the-cells-proposition-alone.md)'s
own four-step test is what raises it.** §41.2 is run here over the one cell §39.9 did not name:

| Step | `5432/tcp`'s footing cell — *the owner's shipped default restricts this pair to loopback* |
| --- | --- |
| **1. Strike A out** | A is `postgresql.conf.sample`'s `listen_addresses`. What remains that this note already cites? |
| **2. Does B alone yield the proposition?** | **[measured] §13.2: `pg_hba.conf.sample` is *"a **second, independent** restricting default"*** — the only shipped `host` records are `127.0.0.1/32` and `::1/128`. §13.2's own verdict: ***"Two restricting defaults are still two defaults."*** **Yes** |
| **3 / 4** | Not reached |

**So step 2 says `5432/tcp` is not an item — and step 2's stated warrant says it is.** The warrant is
*"Two acts are needed to falsify C"*, and **one act falsifies both artefacts**: `postgresql.conf.sample`
and `pg_hba.conf.sample` are two files in one source tree that move on one PostgreSQL major release, at
one rung. **The test measures the second ground's *strength*; the warrant is about the *act's*
multiplicity; and this is the cell where they come apart.** `10255`'s pair does not — a documentation
branch and a shipped default are two acts as well as two artefacts.

**Nothing is ruled here.** Removing `5432/tcp` from the queue would move a figure #135 has just set, on
a reading of #135's own rule, which is exactly the *machine rules* failure §39.6 bars. It is **raised**,
with the criterion that decides it named: **whether *independent* in §39.3 means a second adequate
artefact or a second falsifying act.** The parallel to §41.3 is close and worth stating — #135 found
the note leaning on one **cell** twice; this is the note holding two **artefacts** that one act moves.

> **RULED by [#151](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/151): the act.** Step 2 is corrected
> to require a **different revision act**, not merely a second artefact — [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-a-second-ground-counts-only-where-it-would-have-carried-the-cells-proposition-alone.md)'s
> Amendment. `5432/tcp`'s footing does not move: it was already an item under the removal bar, and the
> act reading confirms it independently. The full register update is §48.

### 40.9 Thin ground, flagged per the standing rule

- **G8's external half is the run's largest hole and it is a hole in the *design*, not in the run.**
  §39.6 calls G8 *closed* on the ground that its re-fetch set is finite and named. **It is finite and
  it is not named** — no section enumerates the citations G8 must re-resolve, and the note carries
  several hundred. The named subset run here was chosen by this section, which is exactly the
  discretion a closed check is supposed to remove. **The criterion that would fix it** is an
  enumeration of G8's population, which is a ticket rather than a reading.

  > **DISCHARGED by §44** ([#150](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/150),
  > [ADR-0088](../adr/0088-a-re-resolution-check-recurs-only-where-its-target-can-move.md)). The
  > population is named, and it is named by a cut nobody had drawn: **a citation is re-resolved every
  > release where its target can move, and checked once where it cannot.** G8-recurring is **36
  > members over 30 owners** (§44.4); G8-entry is ~31 members discharged by the edits that pinned
  > them (§44.5); the internal half is total and mechanical (§44.3). **This run's one external string
  > check falls in the entry half** — it was made *"at the pinned commit"* — so the corpus still holds
  > no measurement of a moving target, which §44.11 raises rather than repairs. §39.6's G8 row is
  > amended at its clause.
- **G11's population was tractable only because the corpus records read-at tags**, and the cell that
  cost most to reach is the cell §36.7 records as *already de-attested once*. `623/udp` sits behind
  two vendor document portals: HPE's returns an **empty body** to plain fetching, being a JavaScript
  application, and Dell's PDF host returns **HTTP 403**. **Neither is a withdrawal and neither is an
  interstitial** — both documents are there and both need a browser — which is §17.10's shell hazard
  arriving from a third direction and the reason this section states the distinction at every site.
  Dell's revision marker, moreover, **appears only on the PDF title page** and never on the HTML
  topic, so the pin cannot be checked from the rendered page at all. **The artefact class the queue
  ranks most volatile is also the class whose currency is hardest to measure**, and those two facts
  are not independent.
- **One forward hazard, recorded rather than acted on.** On the **iLO 7** line HPE has hollowed out
  the Brief's *Ports used by iLO features* section to a pointer — *"see iLO User Guide"* — and moved
  the table to the iLO 7 *User Guide* (PN 30-842B82CC-013). **This note is unaffected**: §36 cites the
  **iLO 6** *User Guide* (`sd00002007en_us`, PN 30-7A345B12-032, July 2026) for the `Direction` table,
  which is a User Guide already and is current. Recorded because the *next* session to reach for a
  ports table in an HPE Security Technology Brief will not find one, and would be at risk of reading
  the absence as a withdrawal.
- **`git.linux-nfs.org` still serves an expired TLS certificate**, reproducing §9.5's recorded hazard
  exactly. `nfs-utils`' current version was taken from `kernel.org`'s own distribution directory
  instead. Recorded because a hazard that reproduces two months later is a property of the source.
- **The eighteen-defect count is a count of *this run's* findings, not of the corpus's defects**, and
  it is as good as the searches that produced it. Shape A was found by grepping two spellings of one
  denominator; shape B by grepping four removed port numbers; shape C by grepping one. **A defect
  phrased in a way none of those matched is not in the count**, and §39.9's warning about the nineteen
  identity sites applies here unchanged and for the same reason.
- **Eight of the eleven checks were decided entirely from bytes already held**, which is the claim
  §39.6 makes for all eleven. The three that needed re-fetching — G7, G10, G11 — needed it in the
  *shape* the design predicts, over named finite sets. **The design's central claim survives its first
  run**, and the one place it does not is G8, above.

### 40.10 Retrieval method and hazards, recorded per §9.5, §11.9, §12.9, §13.10, §14.6, §16.10, §17.10, §22.10, §30.10, §32.13, §33.11, §36.14, §37.14, §38.16 and §39.10

- **Four targeted re-fetches were performed and each is scoped to a check**, per §39.6's *finite named
  set*: G10's list of one, G11's owner release tags, G7's two rendered-artefact comparisons, and one
  G8 string check. **No retrieval here is scoped to a row**, so under ADR-0037 limb 2 **no row can
  move on this section**, and none does.
- **A 404 distinguished from a failure to fetch, deliberately and at every site.** Every absence
  reported above is a server response with a byte count, never an unreachable URL. The one URL that
  could not be reached — `git.linux-nfs.org`, on the expired certificate — is reported as unreached
  and its figure taken from a different owner artefact, with the substitution stated. **Inferring
  withdrawal from a fetch failure is the failure mode this discipline exists to prevent**, and §21.2's
  JavaScript-shell hazard is the same discipline one layer up.
- **G7's own test was applied to G7's own evidence.** The kubelet strings were read from the rendered
  reference **and** from the raw Go source at `v1.36.3`, and the comparison is the finding. A check
  about rendering that read only source would have been unable to fail.
- **Every quoted string attributed to a prior section is quoted from this repository**, so G7 is
  vacuous over this section's internal citations and G8 reduces there to the cross-reference check run
  at §40.5.
- **Sibling passes were editing this repository concurrently**, and this section's basis is `main`
  after [#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135)'s merge, whose §41 it reads and
  applies at §40.7. **Where §40 and §1 disagree, §1 governs.**

## 41. The queue's filter, read at the cell — a second ground counts only where it would have carried the cell's proposition alone

**Ticket [#135](https://github.com/winniel123/verge-asm/issues/135).** §39.9 flagged the sole-ground
filter as the rule's soft edge and named the case: `10250/tcp` is off the queue because
`ports-and-protocols.md`'s `Used By: Self, Control plane` cell counts as a second ground, and §16.9
calls that cell *"the thinnest placement in the table"*. **Nothing in this section is a retrieval.**
Every fact it uses was measured by a prior pass and is cited to it. **No row, class, tier or coverage
figure moves**, and [ADR-0008](../adr/0008-derivation-versions-move-on-content.md) is not triggered. The
reasoning is [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-a-second-ground-counts-only-where-it-would-have-carried-the-cells-proposition-alone.md).

### 41.1 The ruling in one line each

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| **Does a second ground have to be strong enough to have carried the cell alone?** | **Yes** — it must yield **the cell's proposition** with the first artefact struck out. *Exists* is not the bar |
| **What is the cell's proposition** | What the cell asserts **about the world**, stripped of our grading of it. A footing cell: *the owner places this pair inside a boundary it names*. A claim cell: *this named claim from §2.1's closed set holds*. A *why* cell: *the stated ground obtains* |
| **Does the second ground have to reach the same tier?** | **No, and this is the limb that lost.** A footing tier grades **evidential distance** ([ADR-0059](../adr/0059-a-footing-tier-grades-evidential-distance-never-the-owners-conviction.md)) — premises **the reader** supplies. It is our disclosure, not the owner's assertion, so an owner's act cannot falsify it. A fallback at a **lower** tier is a second ground and the act **demotes** |
| **What object is the filter applied to?** | **The cell, never the row.** ADR-0057's unit was already the `(cell, artefact, revision act)` triple; §39.4 disposed of two rows. A row with two cells is tested **twice** |
| **Which way does an undetermined answer fall?** | **On the queue.** An artefact whose status as a ground needs a retrieval is not a ground yet |

### 41.2 The test, stated so #134 can run it

For a cell **C** carried by artefact **A**:

1. **Strike A out.** Ask what C would say on the remaining artefacts this note **already cites** for the row.
2. If some remaining artefact **B**, alone, still yields C's **proposition** — at any tier — B is a second ground and **C is not an item**. Two acts are needed to falsify C.
3. If every remaining artefact yields a **different** proposition — a different cell, a fragment of the cell, or nothing — **C is an item at A's rung**, whatever else the row holds.
4. If step 2 cannot be decided from bytes the project already holds, **C is an item** and the undetermined step is named.

**What does not count as a second ground**, in three shapes the corpus already contains:

| Shape | Instance | Why it is not a ground |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An artefact carrying a **different cell** of the same row | `ports-and-protocols.md` against `10250`'s **footing** cell | §18.6: under ADR-0050 *"the table cell stops carrying the **position** and carries the **membership**"*. Membership is a different proposition — though §18.7 measures that the position **does** fall back to it at the scoping tier, so for `10250`'s footing it is a ground after all (§41.3) |
| An artefact carrying **part** of the proposition | §17.6's two kubelet quotes before §18 ruled | A category statement that does not reach the member yields no proposition about the pair at all |
| A **corroborator** | `2375/tcp`'s Elastic placement (§39.5) | §2.3, unchanged and strictly stronger: a corroborator was never a ground, so it can never remove an item. This rule adds nothing there and takes nothing away |

### 41.3 The worked case — `10250/tcp`, and the flag is discharged on the other cell

**[measured]**, both from sections that ran the measurement:

| Cell | Carried by | Rung | Strike the carrier out | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `10250/tcp` **footing** — *the owner places this pair inside a boundary it names* | `security-checklist.md`'s *"The Kubernetes API, kubelet API and etcd are not exposed publicly on Internet"* | 2 | **§18.7:** *"`10250` falls back to the **scoping tier** on the ports table"*. The proposition survives; the **tier** does not | **Not an item** — a demotion, which is ADR-0057 §3 correctly stated |
| `10250/tcp` **claim** — *Claim 3 holds for this pair* | `ports-and-protocols.md`'s `Used By: Self, Control plane` | 2 | **§19.12:** *"Claim 3 has **no second support** on this row"* | **An item.** §39.4 never tested it, having tested the row |
| `10255/tcp` **footing** — same proposition | the same `security-checklist.md` sentence | 2 | **§18.7:** *"`10255` falls back to the **weak tier** on `readOnlyPort` alone"* | **Not an item** — a demotion. §39.3's disposal is confirmed and re-sited at the cell |

**§39.9's reader is right that `10250` belongs on the queue and wrong about which cell puts it there.**
It is not that the `Used By` cell is too thin to be a ground — it is an adequate ground for the
proposition it carries, and §18.7 measures the footing falling back onto it. It is that **the note leans
on that one cell twice, for two different cells of one row**, and counting it once as a *second* support
for the footing concealed that it is the **only** support for the claim. That is exactly the shape
§39.2 named in the other direction — four pairs on one sentence — arriving as one row on two cells.

> **§39.9's second bullet is DISCHARGED, and §16.9's `10250` flag gains its consequence.** The thin cell
> is on the queue. §19.12's *"the weakness has been promoted from the footing to the claim"* is the
> sentence that decides it, and it was on the record before the queue existed. **No tier moves and no
> row moves** — a queue item is an observation that a cell is exposed, never a verdict on it
> (ADR-0057: *a machine may raise; only a release may rule*).

### 41.4 The queue restated — nine items over eleven pairs and two non-port cells

**§39.4's eight items stand unchanged, with their grounds and their rungs.** This ruling can only add:
it narrows what counts as a second ground and never widens it. One item is added.

| # | Rung | Item — `(cell, artefact, revision act)` | Pairs | Ground |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **9** | **2** | `10250`'s **claim** cell @ `ports-and-protocols.md`'s `Used By: Self, Control plane` — a documentation branch tracking a release line; one contributor, one commit, no release note | `10250/tcp` | **[measured]** §19.12: *"Claim 3 has no second support on this row"*; §16.9, §19.5 |

> **The queue is nine items over eleven `(port, transport)` pairs and two non-port cells** —
> ~~eight items over ten pairs~~, superseded here. The added pair is `10250/tcp`, which is in the **top**
> footing tier, so **three** of the pairs the queue adds beyond the weak tier are top-tier rather than
> two. **The queue's length is still barred as an indicator** (§39.2); it is written down because the
> figure appears at four sites and a stale absolute is what ADR-0058 exists to prevent.

**Still not on the queue, each with its reason restated at the cell:**

| Not an item | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `10250/tcp`'s and `10255/tcp`'s **footing** cells | A second artefact yields the same proposition at a lower tier — §18.7 measures both fallbacks. The act **demotes** |
| `certificate-weak-key-or-signature`'s whole table | Unchanged — **[measured]** [`weak-key-and-signature.md`](./weak-key-and-signature.md) §9.3, a **scope** weakness that silent de-attestation cannot reach |
| Every graded row whose owner sentence **and** configuration artefact yield the **same** proposition | Unchanged, and this is the row the tier-strict reading would have emptied — §41.5. Its members are #134's to enumerate |
| The count of anything | Barred as an indicator — §39.2 |

### 41.5 The option that lost, stated at length because it is the ticket's own candidate

**The candidate was that a second ground must have carried the cell *at its own tier*.** It is the
reading a reader of §16.9 reaches for, it fails in the safe direction, and it is refused on a measurement
and on a warrant.

**The measurement.** §39.4's largest *not an item* row is *"every graded row with an owner sentence
**and** a configuration artefact — two independent acts are needed. **This is most of the list**, which
is why the queue is short."* Every such row has `10255`'s shape: strike the sentence and the row falls to
the weak tier on the shipped default. Under the tier-strict reading **every one of them becomes an
item**, the queue becomes approximately the graded table, and the filter removes nothing — while
ADR-0057 gives support count exactly one job, *"it removes items rather than ordering them"*. A filter
that removes nothing is not a filter, and a reading order that is the whole table is not an order.

**The warrant.**
[ADR-0046](../adr/0046-a-negatives-corpus-is-its-owners-class-list-and-only-a-sole-ground-negative-is-exposed.md)
limb 1 — the arithmetic §39.3 reads on the positive side — is about a claim being **falsified**, not
about it being **re-graded**. ADR-0059 fixes a footing tier as *"the count of premises the reader must
supply"*: it is authored by **us**, about **our** distance. An owner's revision act cannot falsify a
sentence the owner did not write. What the act does is leave our disclosure **over-stated**, and
over-statement of our own distance is the **gate's** business: **G2** walks every graded footing cell
against the tier criterion as it currently stands, and **G11** marks a cell *stale-against-tag* when the
owner's release line moves past the tag the cell was read at.

**A third option, refused for the same reason:** *the second ground must be at least as **strong** as
the first*. Strength is our grading. Ranking grounds by strength re-imports the footing tier as a key
through the filter's back door, one ticket after ADR-0057 refused it as a key through the front — and it
is backwards on the queue's own axis, a weaker artefact at rung 5 being a **better** fallback than a
stronger one at rung 1.

**And the incumbent lost too, which is the finding rather than the ruling.** ADR-0057's words are
*"no second **independent** artefact carries **the same cell**"* — the tighter rule was already written.
What loosened it was applying it to the **row** at §39.4, two subsections after §39.2 fixed the unit as
the cell. **[measured]** the cost of that is one concealed item, and the note contained its own
refutation: §19.12's *"Claim 3 has no second support on this row"* was written before the queue existed.

**Outside this note.**
